content:
mike: FYI canary nodes with NVIDIA driver 540.11 + CUDA 12.3 flipped kernel routing in the autotuner. We saw attn_vec optimized path fall back to generic on short sequences and small batch sizes. p99 for chat-48B up ~10% on canary traffic.
anya: ugh. Is KV cache behavior also impacted or just the attn kernel pick?
mike: Both. Autotuner now prefers a kernel with lower reported gflops but the driver reports higher memory pressure, so kvcache prefetch stride doubled and hitrate dropped. Quick profiler excerpt below.
liam: Paste the snippet and the model/seq/batch config.
mike: Sure:
```
# baseline (driver 537xx)
model: chat-48B | seq=48 | batch=2
kernel: attn_vec_v3  (chosen) | token latency 0.88ms | gflops 340
kvcache: prefetch_stride=64 | hitrate=0.91

# canary (driver 540.11)
model: chat-48B | seq=48 | batch=2
kernel: attn_generic  (chosen) | token latency 0.98ms | gflops 305
kvcache: prefetch_stride=128 | hitrate=0.76
```
anya: That prefetch jump would increase bandwidth and evictions. Did autotune recalc rankings or did driver change cause heuristic shift?
mike: Autotuner ranks kernels by score = latency_est - alpha*gflops - beta*mem_pressure. The driver change alters the mem_pressure probe result, effectively increasing beta*mem_pressure and flipping the score.
ram: Expected after ABI changes. We should have three mitigations: 1) infra rollback of driver on canary, 2) runtime override to prefer attn_vec for specific model/seq ranges, 3) conservative client-side batching temporary.
liam: Ops, is rollback safe? Any disk/state risk?
devops-bot: kubernetes: nodepool/canary-driver rollback started by @mike at 2026-03-18T15:02Z. Nodes will be cordoned->drained->driver-reinstall->uncordon one at a time.
mike: Rolling one node now. Meanwhile I propose a runtime config override to avoid waiting for full rollback. Two short-term options: a per-model kernel preference file or a hotfix to reduce weight of mem_pressure in the score. I prefer the per-model override for narrow scope.
anya: Where would overrides live? Can we hot-reload?
mike: We'll implement a watcher in runtime that reads /etc/redwood/kernel_overrides.yaml and applies per-model rules without restart. Example file:
```
chat-48B: { max_seq: 64, prefer: attn_vec_v3 }
qa-7B: { prefer: attn_generic, min_batch: 8 }
```
liam: Good. Also add telemetry: record kernel_pick_reason tag (autotune, override, heuristic) and seq bucket histogram so we can see impact by sequence length.
ram: Long-term: add per-driver calibration offsets to autotuner; on model onboarding run a short micro-benchmark that stores driver-specific mem_pressure/latency deltas.
mike: I'll open two PRs: one for kernel_overrides watcher + telemetry, and one infra job that runs a synthetic seq=8..128 sweep after any driver bumps in canary.
anya: Can you also collect NV counters for memory bandwidth and PCIe stalls from the nodes so we can correlate with prefetch stride?
mike: Yep collecting nv-nsight and /proc/nv_gpu samples. Early numbers: after rolling node-1 back to driver 537xx its p99 improved ~5% vs remaining canary nodes.
devops-bot: nodepool/canary-driver rollback completed for node-1 at 2026-03-18T15:18Z. Node rejoined cluster.
liam: What about automated tests? We should block driver upgrades on a canary regression gate that replays short-seq synthetic workload and fails the rollout if p99 regresses >3% or kvcache hitrate drops >5% vs baseline.
ram: Agreed. Add that gate to infra CI and to the cloud provider upgrade playbook. Also add an annotation in release notes about potential kernel ranking sensitivity.
mike: Plan and timeline: 1) finish rolling remaining canary nodes (in progress) 2) land kernel_overrides watcher PR (hot image in ~30m) 3) deploy runtime image to canary behind feature flag 4) enable telemetry and watch kernels/p99/kvcache histograms 5) promote when stable.
anya: Reminder: keep canary traffic at <=25% until metrics stable.
liam: Also consider a small runtime change to clamp prefetch_stride when hitrate falls below threshold to avoid runaway memory thrash. Might be too invasive for emergency but worth a follow-up.
ram: I'll create a follow-up ticket: AUTOTUNE-4279 for per-driver offsets + AUTOTUNE-4280 for prefetch clamp.
mike: Opening PRs now, will post links here. Thanks folks. :thumbsup:
anya: Thanks Mike. Keep posting updates in this thread.
liam: Nice quick containment.
ram: Good catch on telemetry requirement.
mike: update: kernel_overrides watcher PR merged to canary branch and image pushed at 2026-03-18T15:42Z. Deploying to canary nodes behind flag.
devops-bot: rollout: runtime/canary-image@sha256:abcd started at 2026-03-18T15:47Z to nodes: node-2,node-3.
mike: Early telemetry after override: kernel_pick_reason shows 90% overrides for chat-48B seq<65; p99 moved back within 2% of baseline; kvcache hitrate recovered to 0.88.
anya: Great. We can keep kernel override as short-term emergency control while we implement per-driver calibration.
liam: After we finish drivers rollouts, schedule a postmortem and adjust canary gate.
ram: Filing postmortem ticket now.
mike: Will close loop once prod promotion done.
